source.title: When Are Sparse Feature Interventions Actually Localized? Matched Evaluation for SAE-Based Safety Control

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAE features as intervention handles and evaluates their safety-control performance. It does not test superposition geometry, feature sparsity or importance, polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete, canonical representation units.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition as motivation, but its experiments measure intervention effects and costs, not the representation claims in the listed versions. Rows below record intervention findings relevant to sparse-feature control; they do not test any listed version. Cited results from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper uses Gemma Scope and Llama Scope SAE features as ablation handles. It evaluates their safety-control efficiency against dense steering: true-jailbreak rate, capability and perturbation. Superposition appears only as background motivation in Section 2.1. No experiment measures feature geometry, sparsity transitions, capacity-driven polysemanticity, neuron distribution, SAE feature completeness or canonicality, or feature dimensionality. The split-overlap result (R20) concerns the stability of a cosine-similarity ranking of features against a refusal direction. It is not about whether the SAE's features are stable or canonical units of the model, so it does not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors find the comparison direction-dependent: for refusal injection, dense steering preserves capability better. They also find that high-k SAE ablations, and SAE ablations in the 2B model, inflate a single safety judge with incoherent or non-completing outputs. They recommend matched-surface, matched-basis, coherence-gated, multi-judge evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Inference-time SAE feature ablation and dense activation steering for safety-control evaluation; not a reproduction of the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported intervention comparison changes with model scale and architecture, dense-baseline surface and basis, intervention direction, and SAE feature count. The 27B result uses a 4-bit checkpoint; the paper reports three seeds for that scale point.

fits_no_version.finding: On Gemma-2-9B, the SAE ablation advantage over all-layer dense steering at matched perturbation (+0.094 to +0.104) reverses against same-layer dense and decoder-span-projected dense baselines (up to −0.286).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Apparent sparse-feature intervention efficiency depends on matching the dense baseline's intervention surface and basis, not just total perturbation norm.

fits_no_version.finding: Against all-layer dense steering, SAE ablation retains large advantages on Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-27B. On Gemma-2-2B it comes with large capability collapse, and the HarmBench second judge does not corroborate it (κ→0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE safety-intervention effects and costs vary with model scale and architecture; small-model SAE steering results may not transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal-aligned SAE feature separation decays with rank, and the top800 set overlaps substantially across splits. Single-feature ablations have tiny effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this setting, effective SAE control of refusal is distributed over a medium-k group of features rather than carried by a single feature.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says materials will be publicly released and are available from the authors on request until then
record.problems: The authors describe the perturbation measure as a proxy for locality, not proof of causal isolation. The 27B run has three seeds, uses 4-bit weights, and omits capability comparisons. Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-27B comparisons use an all-layer dense baseline rather than surface-matched baselines. The human audit is targeted and single-annotator.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the reported capability metrics, judge agreement, coherence audit, refusal-injection direction, raw Pareto results, or auxiliary retain-set results: these report safety-control performance or evaluation artifacts rather than any listed representation claim. The key matched comparisons and feature diagnostics are retained above.

untested.parts: Toy networks, feature-to-dimension ratio, overlapping near-orthogonal storage, sparsity-dependent transition, geometry: none tested.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions: not tested.
Non-capacity origins of polysemantic neurons: not tested.
Whether features are spread across neurons, or whether SAEs recover sparse features as evidence about LLM representations: not tested. SAEs are used only as intervention tools.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features as model units: not tested. Ranking overlap across prompt splits (R20) is a selection-stability diagnostic, not a test of the dictionary.
One-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features: not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Correctly gated as T4 with no verdicts. All rows correctly map to no version; only state corrections are needed (R4 non-significant; R21/R22 lack baselines). The paper's 'rank-decay geometry' language refers to the ranking of features by cosine similarity to a refusal direction, not to representational superposition geometry.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature count relative to dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features as evidence about the underlying representation.
The study uses SAE features but does not test whether they are complete, canonical units of the model’s representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
